newsitem.title: USA: Tandy posts sharp profit drop, cites tough retail market.
newsitem.headline: Tandy posts sharp profit drop, cites tough retail market.

text.p: Tandy Corp., the parent of RadioShack, Computer City, and Incredible Universe, Thursday reported a sharp drop in quarterly earnings, citing a difficult consumer electronics retail market.
The company said earnings fell to $22.3 million, or 35 cents a share, in the third quarter, compared with profits of $45.0 million or 66 cents a share a year earlier.
Sales rose to $1.43 billion from $1.34 billion.

"The results announced today reflect a tough consumer electronics retail environment that the industry has been experiencing," John V. Roach, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a brief statement accompanying the results.
Earlier this month the company said that third-quarter sales at RadioShack and Incredible Universe were among the best in the consumer electronics business although they were below year-ago levels.
Tandy has 6,800 RadioShack stores and 112 Computer City stores, as well as 17 Incredible Universe outlets.
The company's stock was off 37.5 cents at $39.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
